u0: Base/final calm state: no siren or pot emergency is demanding action, and no fallen-food recovery is pending. Continue the ordinary shop routine—take a waiting client's order, fetch raw food from the pantry if needed, prepare it at the stove, and serve—while staying ready to switch immediately if a siren, boil, or food slip occurs.
u1: Siren emergency: the siren is ringing and has priority over the pot and routine work. Go to the siren switch and toggle it off as soon as possible; a quick serve of already prepared food is still rewarded, but the state remains siren-active until the switch is toggled. If the pot is also boiling, handle it only after silencing the siren.
u10: Pot-boiling emergency with the siren silent: go to the stove. If carrying food, first drop it on a free adjacent cell, toggle the stove down with empty hands, then pick the food back up; if already empty-handed, toggle the stove directly. Keep the fix as the top priority, though serving already prepared food is compatible; a new siren switches to the siren-response state.
u2: Immediate food-recovery state with the siren silent: the carried food has just slipped and is on the floor, so your hands are empty. On the very next move, turn toward and pick up that food; picking it up resolves the recovery, returning to routine or to the pot/siren state if another hazard is active. Taking another action instead moves into the persistent lost-food state with penalties.
u3: Immediate food-recovery state while the siren is ringing: the food has just slipped, your hands are empty, and the siren is on. Recover the fallen food on the next move if possible; picking it up leaves the siren still active. If the switch is immediately at hand, silencing the siren is also useful, but do not spend an idle step—failure to recover at once moves to the persistent lost-food-and-siren state.
u4: Persistent dropped-food state with the siren silent: your hands are empty and the fallen food is still on the floor. Recover it promptly—each idle step that leaves you empty-handed keeps the loss active and penalized. Once the food is in hand, the machine returns to the ordinary routine or to the pot/siren emergency if one is now active; if the siren starts before recovery, move to the lost-food-plus-siren state.
u5: Persistent dropped-food state with the siren ringing: hands are empty, food remains on the floor, and the siren is still on. Address both promptly: silence the siren when at the switch, and pick up the fallen food as soon as possible; idle empty-handed steps are penalized. After either interruption is cleared, finish the other and return to routine.
u6: Just-fixed-the-stove state with the siren silent: the pot has been turned down and is no longer boiling, but your hands are empty because fixing the stove required empty hands. Retrieve any food you set down beside the stove immediately, then resume routine client and order work; a newly active siren or pot should take over as the next emergency.
u7: Just-fixed-the-stove state while the siren is ringing: the pot is down, but the siren remains active and your hands are empty. Next silence the siren; as soon as possible also pick up any food you put down to free your hands, then resume routine work. The stove is no longer the urgent problem.
u8: Post-stove-fix follow-up with the siren silent: the pot has been handled and you are still empty-handed. If food was set aside for the fix, pick it up now; otherwise return to the normal client workflow, taking or serving orders as appropriate. This is a short aftermath state—new siren or pot activity should immediately become the priority.
u9: Post-stove-fix follow-up while the siren still rings: the pot has been handled, but the siren is active and your hands are empty. Silence the siren next, and collect any food set aside for the stove repair when possible; then return to the normal shop loop.
